subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up / Paywise - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paywise.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: encryption, KMS/HSM options + next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align with Paywise security requirements.

Summary of your requirements (as discussed):
- PII handling: ensure request/response data containing PII is protected and can be excluded from logging; need clarity on token-level traces and whether any request content is persisted.
- Data retention: default logs retained for 30 days; Paywise requires configurable retention down to 0 days and the ability to request immediate purge for selected datasets.
- Logging controls: need an option to disable request/response logging and/or redact PII prior to storage.
- Data residency: primary region us-west-2; some backup copies must stay in the US.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS, at-rest AES-256, and preference for customer-managed keys (CMEK). Consideration for HSM-backed keys for high-assurance workloads.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced for all endpoints and internal service-to-service traffic.
- At-rest: AES-256 with envelope encryption. We support CMEK across hosted and Dedicated via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
- HSM/BYOK: for Private deployments we support integration with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) and can offer HSM-backed keys for Dedicated through vetted partners.
- Logging/Retention: configurable logging controls — can disable request-body logging, redact tokens, or set retention windows per-tenant. We also offer a manual purge process for specific datasets.

Attachments: redwood_kms_whitepaper.pdf (details on CMEK/HSM flows), customer-data-security-sheet.xlsx (matrix of logging and retention controls).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share the whitepaper and a short FAQ answering your security team’s questions.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our security engineer (Neha) and solutions engineer (Dylan) to walk through key rotation, BYOK, and HSM integration.
3) If helpful, we can prepare a limited-run PoC in us-west-2 with CMEK enabled.

Are you available for a technical session Friday morning (PT)? If not, suggest two times next week and I’ll lock it in.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paywise.com>

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: encryption, KMS/HSM options + next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security team (copied):

1) Token-level logging: we need to confirm whether any token-level traces (model input/output tokens) are retained by default. Can you confirm if token traces are stored and if they can be disabled per-tenant?
2) PII in responses: if the model outputs PII that we later flag, can we request data removal and is there a documented purge SLA?
3) CMEK scope: for hosted (Redwood API) can we use our AWS KMS CMKs or do we need Dedicated/Private for full BYOK? If hosted supports CMEK, what are the limitations?
4) HSM requirement: for certain regulated flows we need an HSM-backed key that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or equivalent). Do you support HSMs that meet that level, and how does key escrow/rotation work?
5) Key egress: will keys ever leave our KMS/HSM? We need assurance that private key material is never exported.

Also — retention: our baseline requirement is 0-7 days for logs containing PII unless otherwise agreed; is that configurable today?

If you can answer these prior to the technical call, that would help focus the session.

Best,
Alex Turner
Director, Platform Security | Paywise
alex.turner@paywise.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paywise.com>
Cc: Paywise Security <security@paywise.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: encryption, KMS/HSM options + next steps

Alex — great questions. See answers below; I’ve kept them short and can expand in the technical deep-dive.

1) Token-level logging: by default our hosted API captures minimal request metadata and request IDs for observability, but we do not persist full token-level traces for customers unless "debug logging" is explicitly enabled. For Paywise we can disable debug-level token traces and ensure only hashed request IDs exist in logs. This is configurable per-tenant.

2) PII in responses & purge: we support an on-demand purge workflow for request/response content. If Paywise flags specific items as PII, we can remove them within our standard purge SLA (48 hours for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private SLAs can be tightened). We also provide a redaction pipeline to remove PII before persistent storage in cases where you want to avoid retention entirely.

3) CMEK scope (hosted vs Dedicated): hosted Redwood API supports CMEK for encryption of persisted artifacts via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault (CMEK). There are operational constraints on hosted CMEK: you retain key control, but we perform envelope encryption and use short-lived data keys that are not exportable. For full HSM-backed BYOK (where key material never leaves customer control), Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended. We can outline tradeoffs in the call.

4) HSM / FIPS: we integrate with validated HSM vendors (Thales/Luna, AWS CloudHSM) and can support FIPS 140-2 Level 2+ and Level 3 options depending on deployment. For Private deployments we can enable customer-managed HSMs where keys never leave the device. For Dedicated, we can work with CloudHSM partners to meet higher assurance needs.

5) Key egress: Redwood never requires export of your private key material. For CMEK we use envelope encryption and short-lived data keys; for BYOK/HSM integrations keys are non-exportable and operations use remote cryptographic calls (e.g., KMS Encrypt/Decrypt, HSM sign).

Retention: retention windows are configurable per-tenant; we can set PII-containing logs to 0-7 days per your requirement and enable redaction to avoid persistence.

Attachments: SLA_Annex.pdf (sample encryption annex), redwood_kms_whitepaper.pdf (already shared).

Next steps:
- Neha and Dylan to join a 60m technical call to walk key rotation, audit logs (who can see key usage), and HSM proofs.
- I’ll share our SOC2 summary and a list of HSM FIPS certs prior to the call.

Proposed times: Fri 2027-05-21 09:00-10:00 PT or Mon 2027-05-24 11:00-12:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — Marissa
